• Problem 4 occurs because without a coverslip to barrier the wet specimen, focusing down with the high-power (×40) objective lens—which has a very short working distance—can cause the lens to touch the liquid iodine stain, contaminating or scratching the objective lens.
• Problem 2 does not occur because iodine solution stains chromatin and starch inside cells, making the nuclei clearly visible under a light microscope.

• In leukaemia (a cancer of blood-forming stem cells in the bone marrow), uncontrolled mitotic cell division leads to hyperactive bone marrow function (increased) and releases abnormally large numbers of immature white blood cells (increased).
• In measles (an infectious viral disease), the body mounts an active immune response, stimulating the proliferation of lymphocytes and other leukocytes to fight the virus, which increases the white blood cell count.
Therefore, all three parameters (leukaemia WBC count, leukaemia bone marrow function, and measles WBC count) are increased.
